messages:
kai: Heads-up — we've started seeing intermittent NCCL jobs aborting with OOB timeouts after last night's host kernel and firmware rollouts in us-west-2. Happens only for multi-node jobs (4+ GPUs) that use RoCE paths.
maria: Any logs / error lines? short repro?
kai: Pasted from one of the failed workers: ```[2026-03-17 02:14:08] NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send failed: ret=-1 errno=110, OOB timeout
[2026-03-17 02:14:09] NCCL INFO Retry connect to rank 2, attempt 3
[2026-03-17 02:14:15] NCCL FATAL unhandled error, aborting```.
tj: Thanks. Can you share ethtool and ibv_devinfo outputs from the host that failed? Also any ToR counters (drops/port errors)?
kai: Quick dumps attached inline: ```# ethtool -S eno1 | grep drop
rx_drops: 1342
# ibv_devinfo -v | head -n5
device: mlx5_2
transport: InfiniBand
# dmesg | tail -n20
mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: WARNING: RoCE packet reordering detected, seq_mismatch=8
```.
infra-oncall: We rolled kernel from 6.1.14 -> 6.2.9 and mlx5 firmware to fw-41. Could be new Rx coalescing defaults. Any recent changes to ToR?
maria: Networking said nothing changed on ToR config but there was a jumbo MTU auto-negotiation tweak last week on the aggregation layer (we're checking). If host MTU < ToR due to negotiation it can lead to fragmentation and drops for RDMA.
sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0317-07 (probable RoCE reordering). Adding infra-oncall and net team.
tj: Short mitigation: can we force the host to the previous mlx5 driver/firmware or disable Rx LRO/GRO and set MTU forcibly to 9216 on hosts involved? Also try forcing IB VQ pairs to 'preferred' mode in osh-runbook to avoid out-of-order handling.
kai: Will try: running `sudo ethtool -K eno1 gro off lro off tso off` and `sudo ip link set eno1 mtu 9216`. Also toggled `sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=268435456`.
(5m later) kai: After disabling GRO/LRO + forcing MTU 9216 on the two problematic hosts, the job ran 20 minutes without OOB timeouts before we aborted test. Packet drop counters went down from ~1300 -> 6.
maria: Good signal. Net team is going to verify ToR MTU negotiation logs and check if the aggregation tweak caused asymmetric MTU during flaps. If confirmed we'll schedule rollback and plan a controlled fw/driver bump.
infra-oncall: Plan: (1) revert kernel/firmware in canary pool and run overnight stress, (2) keep GRO/LRO disabled and MTU pinned in affected pools until net confirms, (3) add RDMA-specific link healthmonitor to alert on seq_mismatch and ibv errors.
tj: Also add a short NCCL config change to prefer TCP fallback for OOB comms in case RDMA reordering happens during maintenance windows: set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0? (need validation).
sre-bot: Adding runbook note with commands we used and observed counters. TAGS: rdma, nccl, roce, mtu, fw-rollout.
kai: Thanks — will follow up with logs from full revert test.
